title.rendered: Say to This Mountain: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Whoever says to this mountain, Be removed and be cast into the sea, and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that those things he says will be done, he will have whatever he says. Jesus put the authority in the mouth of the believer.

content.rendered:
Whoever says to this mountain, “Be removed and be cast into the sea,” and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that those things he says will be done, he will have whatever he says. Jesus put the authority in the mouth of the believer. Say. Not just pray. Say.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, July 30, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“So Jesus answered and said to them, ‘Have faith in God. For assuredly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, “Be removed and be cast into the sea,” and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that those things he says will be done, he will have whatever he says. Therefore I say to you, whatever things you ask when you pray, believe that you receive them, and you will have them.'”
Mark 11:22-24 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Mark 11 records one of Jesus’ most direct teachings on how faith actually operates in the life of the believer. The disciples had just watched the fig tree Jesus cursed the day before wither from the roots. Peter marvelled at what had happened in twenty-four hours. Jesus’ response is one of the most quoted, and most often misunderstood, sentences in His entire teaching ministry. Have faith in God. Say to the mountain. Do not doubt in your heart. Believe. Whatever you say, you will have.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition expands the passage: “Have faith in God [constantly]. Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, Be lifted up and thrown into the sea! and does not doubt at all in his heart but believes that what he says will take place, it will be done for him” (Mark 11:22-23 AMPC). Constantly. Have faith constantly. Not occasionally. Not when the mountain looks removable. Constantly.

The Passion Translation renders Jesus’ words with striking clarity: “Have faith in God. Listen to the truth I speak to you: Whoever says to this mountain with great faith and does not doubt, ‘Mountain, be lifted up and thrown into the midst of the sea,’ and believes that what he says will happen, it will be done” (Mark 11:22-23 TPT). Notice what Jesus emphasises. The saying. The words. The believer speaks to the mountain. The mountain does not speak to the believer.

This is the shift most believers never quite make. When we face a mountain, our instinct is to speak about the mountain. To describe it. To complain about it. To catalogue how large it is. Jesus tells us to reverse the direction of our speech. Speak to the mountain. Not about it. And what we say must be aligned with what Jesus has already said. Move. Be removed. In the name of Jesus. The mountain has no legal authority to remain where the King has commanded it to move.

For Gospelbuzz readers, this is one of the most practical exercises of the believer’s authority. Whatever mountain is in front of you today, speak to it in the name of Jesus. Not with your own strength. With the authority of the King who has already commanded it. And do not doubt in your heart. Believe. Say what you believe. Not what you fear. Not what your circumstances show. Not what the enemy is suggesting. Say what the Word of God has said. And, on the schedule of the Father who governs all things, you shall have what you say.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have placed authority in my mouth to speak to mountains in the name of Jesus. I refuse to spend today describing the mountain. I speak to the mountain today. Be removed. In the name of Jesus. I do not doubt in my heart. I believe what You have said. What my words agree with is what will come to pass, because the Word of God on my lips carries the authority of the King. Every mountain that stands in the way of Your purpose for my life, be removed in Jesus’ name. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I speak to mountains in the name of Jesus. I do not describe them. I command them. What I say, aligned with the Word of God, is what shall come to pass.
